newsitem.title: USA: Prosecution lays out Oklahoma bomb case for jurors.
newsitem.headline: Prosecution lays out Oklahoma bomb case for jurors.

text.p: Prosecutors on Thursday began their case against Timothy McVeigh, accused of murder and conspiracy in the April 1995 bombing of a U.S. government building in Oklahoma City that killed 168 people.
Chief prosecutor Joseph Hartzler began by setting the scene, telling jurors that April 19, 1995, was a beautiful day in Oklahoma City and "the sun was shining."
Security was heavy around the federal complex housing the courthouse in downtown Denver and mounted police patrolled the area in a heavy snowstorm.
Spectators lined up by 6:30 a.m. MDT (8:30 a.m. EDT), 2-1/2 hours before the session was scheduled to begin, to get one of the coveted seats in the courtroom.
McVeigh, who turned 29 on Wednesday, is accused of bombing the Alfred P. Murrah federal building, killing 168 people, including 19 children.

The jury of 12 jurors and six alternates was sworn in just after 9 a.m. MDT (11 a.m. EDT). Federal Judge Richard Matsch told them a television camera in the courtroom did not show their faces and was only telecasting the proceedings by closed circuit to Oklahoma City.
